title: Oncall Bridgelet: compact incident dossier surfaced between alert card and postmortem
creator: Mateo Ruiz
description: Problem: on-call responders often need a fast, low-distraction summary when opening an alert in the Console. Current alert-detail flows require multiple clicks and context switches to reach runbooks, postmortems, or recent SLO deltas. Goal: design a compact, scannable 'bridgelet' — a transient dossier that attaches to an alert card and surfaces critical handoff artifacts (recent incident summary, pinned runbooks, postmortem link, SLO snapshot, cost delta) without leaving the alert list.
acceptance_criteria: Bridgelet opens from an alert row and overlays adjacent content without navigating to a new page
Includes: 1-line incident summary, top 2 relevant runbook links, link to latest postmortem, SLO delta sparkline (last 24h), and estimated cost delta for the incident
Keyboard accessible: open/close via Enter and Escape, focus trap while open
Performance: opening animation under 120ms on typical laptop (measured in prototype runs)
UX copy reviewed and approved by SRE team and PM
Figma prototype and accessibility spec published in Confluence
design_notes: Surface prioritization: emphasize runbook + postmortem link first for incident recovery, then SLO and cost context secondary
Layout: compact two-column grid on wide screens, stacked for narrow widths. Keep height under 220px for single glance readability
Interaction: ephemeral by default (closes on blur) but can be pinned to open the full incident view
Privacy: do not expose sensitive customer identifiers in the bridgelet summary by default — show hashed ids and require clickthrough to view full details
Fallback: when no postmortem exists, surface 'Create postmortem' CTA that opens the standard postmortem modal
decisions: Use a transient overlay (bridgelet) rather than inline expansion to avoid shifting list layout and accidental context loss
Prioritize content density over visual ornamentation to support first-response speed
Show SLO delta as micro-sparkline + numeric percent; clicking the sparkline navigates to SLO timeline in a new tab
Expose a lightweight 'handoff note' composer in the bridgelet so responders can drop a 1-2 line update without leaving the view
next_steps: Finalize microcopy and handoff-note character limit with PM (deadline 2026-03-15)
Handoff to Eng for accessibility review and performance budget (ENG-1842) — include prototype LCP timings
A/B test: compare bridgelet vs existing flow for mean time to ack on a sample org for 2 weeks
Prepare rollout plan for beta orgs via feature flag in console-2026.04 release
links: SLO dashboard sample used for sparkline: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/alerts/slo-recent
comments: 2026-02-02 - Mateo Ruiz: Initial wireframes attached to PRD. Leaned toward a 2-column micro-layout to fit both runbooks and SLO sparkline without scrolling.

2026-02-18 - Ava Chen: Usability round 1 with three oncall volunteers. Key feedback: handoff-note composer felt useful but should default to 'private' unless user toggles; pin affordance needs clearer iconography.

2026-02-25 - PM (Rina Patel): Confirmed cost delta is required for billing-sensitive customers. PM suggests showing absolute and percent change; engineering flagged extra API call cost — added to ENG-1842 to evaluate caching.

2026-03-03 - UX Research (Samir Kaur): Prototype moderated test (n=12) showed 35% faster time-to-first-action with bridgelet vs baseline. Participants preferred ephemeral overlay that didn't navigate away.
2026-03-10 - Engineering review (Liu Zhang): Performance note — prefetch minimal incident metadata on hover to reduce open latency. Will add prefetch flag behind feature toggle in GH PR #6218.
2026-03-12 - Design review (Ava Chen): Updated Figma with accessible color variants and keyboard flows. Ready for engineering handoff pending final microcopy and edge-case spec for private incidents.
